title: Limpet Teeth Are Stronger Than Spider Silk

scenes.text: In 2015, scientists found the strongest natural material in a snail's tooth.
It's the limpet, a small sea snail that clings to rocks.
Its teeth are under a millimeter long.
But they beat spider silk, the old record holder.
They're packed with tiny fibers of an iron mineral.
The limpet uses them to scrape food off hard rock. The strongest natural material? A snail's tooth.

description:
In 2015, scientists found the strongest natural material in a snail's tooth.
Limpet teeth contain tiny fibers of an iron mineral and measured stronger than spider silk.
What's the toughest thing you know of in nature?
first_comment: Engineers want to copy this tooth. What should they build with it?
